memory_update.text: WEST is the cleanest US-listed direct exposure found for the B2B coffee/tea/extract/private-label beverage solutions node, but follow-up must focus on profitability, leverage, Conway utilization, and commodity pass-through quality.

FARM and JVA are direct but micro-cap speculative exceptions; both require strict liquidity, balance-sheet, cash-flow, customer concentration, and exchange-listing checks before moving beyond Layer 1.

The node has two distinct public-market mappings: integrated beverage solutions/co-manufacturing platforms like WEST, and route-based foodservice coffee/tea distributors like FARM. These should be scored separately in later layers.

Private competitors and customers such as Ventura Foods, Golden State Foods, restaurant chains, Sysco, and US Foods may reveal demand and customer-dependency signals even when the direct supplier is not public.

node: B2B coffee, tea, extracts, and private-label beverage solutions
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for B2B coffee, tea, extracts, and private-label beverage solutions. The strongest direct public exposure found is Westrock Coffee, which explicitly reports integrated coffee, tea, flavors, extracts, ingredients, foodservice, restaurant, private-label, and RTD manufacturing exposure. Farmer Bros. and Coffee Holding are smaller, more obscure direct coffee/tea foodservice and private-label suppliers but carry micro-cap/speculative balance-sheet and execution risk. Keurig Dr Pepper is included only as a reference leader because it anchors single-serve coffee systems and away-from-home/foodservice context, but its market cap and brand mix make it less suitable for the underfollowed lane.
